title: Black Hills plans $1.8 billion investment to power Google's data center
source_used: Reuters bullet summary as carried by The Economic Times
key_facts: Black Hills Corp, a South Dakota-based utility, said on 6 Oct 2026 it signed agreements to power a proposed Google data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming.
It plans to spend $1.8 billion from 2027 to 2029 on new generation capacity, including 564 MW built for the project.
The project is expected to draw on a 2.7 GW resource mix including reserve margins; deliveries begin in late 2027 and peak load is expected in 2030.

Black Hills supplies up to 590 MW from the grid, mostly from a new gas plant at its Cheyenne Prairie Generating Station, and manages about 2.1 GW of third-party resources through a privately managed microgrid.
It expects the project to add about $150 million to net income by 2030.
Google must cover the full cost of supplying the electricity, so costs are not passed to other utility customers.
quote_evidence: The agreement requires Google to cover the full cost of supplying electricity to the data center, preventing those expenses from being passed on to other utility customers
